_comment: The config.toml form codex-cli takes for auto-approving ONE tool of ONE MCP server,
observed by running the host and writing down what it did. Nothing here was read out of it.
Codex asks the user to approve every call to an MCP tool by default. A
that one tool run without the ask, and every other tool of the same server keeps asking.
`scripts/setup.mjs` writes this form for the two tools in `tools`, and for no other. They
are the two the outcome review asks the model to call, so without them a turn that showed
a lesson would raise an approval prompt every time the review ran.
`toml` is exactly what setup is expected to leave under the `mubit` server's own table.
`codex-setup.test.mjs` feeds it to the host (`codex mcp get`) to show the host reads the
key: the same table with a value the host does not know fails to load the config at all,
naming the key's path, so the key is validated rather than ignored.
Not written by setup: `default_tools_approval_mode` on the server's own table. It is the
server-wide key, and approving every Mubit tool is not what the user is asked to accept.

how: Two `codex exec` sessions in a throwaway CODEX_HOME holding only a copy of the credential,
with recorder hooks on PreToolUse, PermissionRequest and PostToolUse (trust granted the way
setup grants it), and a stdio MCP server named `mubit` exposing two tools, `mubit_outcome`
and `mubit_recall`. The prompt called each tool once.
with no PermissionRequest; mubit_recall raised one. Without it: both raised one.
Config load checked with `codex mcp get mubit --json` against the same table.
